title: Intermittent over-aggressive scale-down causing cold starts and latency spikes (postmortem)
creator: Maya Patel
description: During two short production traffic peaks on 2026-02-23 and 2026-02-24, a subset of inference worker pools experienced repeated cold starts and elevated 95th-percentile latency. The immediate effect was increased error rates and slower completions for a set of customer routes that require single-digit tail latency. The incident surface area: hosted API route group 'gen/large' handling bursty PLG traffic and a dedicated pool serving a high-volume enterprise tenant.
impact_summary: Aggregate 95th latency for affected routes rose from 75ms baseline to 1.2s for ~12 minutes across two events. Error rate (5xx) increased from 0.1% to 2.8% during the incidents. Customer support opened 8 escalations; two customers reported degraded user experience. Estimated 8k excess token-rendering seconds billed during the event due to repeated cold start tokens.
detection: Alerting fired from the console: 'instance-provision-failure' and 'p95-latency-above-500ms' pager alerts. On-call noticed repeated scale events followed by immediate scale-downs within 20-45s and a surge of container restarts. Engineers correlated scale transcripts with KEDA scaler logs and our custom queue-length exporter metrics.
timeline:
- 2026-02-23 09:42 UTC: First short traffic spike observed.
- 09:43:00: KEDA triggers scale up (+6 pods).
- 09:43:50: Scale down initiated (pods removed) due to scaleDownCooldown=30s and exporter returning stale low queue values.
- 09:44-09:50: Repeated up/down cycles; p95 latency climbs.
- 10:05: Incident mitigated by manual scale override and temporary increase to scaleDownCooldown=180s.
- 2026-02-24 14:11 UTC: Second similar spike, repeat behaviour observed.
- 14:25: Autoscaler tuning patch deployed and rollout validated in staging before prod patch at 14:55.
- 2026-02-24 16:00: Postmortem investigation kickoff and data collection completed.
root_cause: A race between KEDA custom scaler evaluation and our queue-length exporter caused transient 'false low' metric values when the exporter aggregated counters across recent short bursts. Combined factors: (1) exporter scrapes and aggregation window defaulted to 5s causing staleness on sub-1min bursts; (2) KEDA's scaleDownCooldown was set to 30s which was too short given instance cold-start latency; (3) aggressive horizontalPodAutoscaler target utilization thresholds allowed immediate scale-down during queue dips. Result: the autoscaler repeatedly removed capacity shortly after provisioning, causing repeated cold starts and tail latency spike.
contributing_factors:
- Short exporter aggregation window (5s) leading to noisy low metrics.
- scaleDownCooldown shorter than cold-start time.
- No heartbeat metric to indicate 'recent scale-up in progress' to the scaler.
- Lack of synthetic burst testing for the specific queue/route shape.
- Runbook escalation path didn't include quick manual hold scale action until mitigations were applied.
actions_taken_during_incident:
- Manual hold of scale-down (temporary override) to stabilize capacity.
- Increased scaleDownCooldown to 180s as emergency mitigation.
- Rolled a config change to exporter to increase aggregation window to 20s in prod staging and then prod.
- Enabled a KEDA fallback scaler that uses CPU when queue metrics are inconsistent.
action_items: A1: Increase default exporter aggregation window from 5s to 20s for queue-length metrics (owner: infra/metrics, ETA: 2026-03-03)
A2: Set KEDA scaleDownCooldown to 180s for inference pools that have cold-start latency > 500ms (owner: serving/runtime, ETA: 2026-03-05)
A3: Add a 'recent_scale_up' heartbeat metric emitted for 5 minutes after any scale-up; scalers should consider heartbeat before scaling down (owner: serving/runtime, ETA: 2026-03-10)
A4: Implement multi-signal scaling policy in KEDA: require either queue_length OR CPU above threshold for scale-down decisions, not just queue_length (owner: runtime-autoscale, ETA: 2026-03-12)
A5: Create automated chaos test in staging that simulates 30s microbursts and validates no oscillation (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-15)
A6: Update runbooks with a 'hold scale-down' quick action and add a playbook for repeated up/down oscillations (owner: SRE/On-call, ETA: 2026-03-04)
A7: Add an alert 'keda-scaler-inconsistent-metric' when scaler sees >3 conflicting metric reports in 2m (owner: observability, ETA: 2026-03-08)
A8: Schedule a post-deploy smoke test window after autoscaler/config changes for 24h to monitor regressions (owner: platform-eng, ETA: 2026-03-06)

A9: Evaluate long-term: replace custom queue exporter with a dedicated, strongly-consistent metric pipeline or use server-side queue length computed in the serving runtime (owner: metrics-architecture, ETA: 2026-04-01)
A10: Document cost impact and notify billing/product for customer credits where appropriate (owner: finance+support, ETA: 2026-03-07)
A11: Run a calibration experiment in staging to find optimal scaleDownCooldown per model size and region (owner: runtime-performance, ETA: 2026-03-20)
verification_plan:
- Deploy exporter window change to staging; run synthetic microburst tests and verify no oscillation.
- Monitor p95 latency and scale event counts for 48h after prod rollout.
- Confirm heartbeat metric is emitted and scalers respect it before any scale-down.
- Validate alerts fire for simulated inconsistent metrics.
follow_up_meetings: 2026-03-03 15:00 UTC: Postmortem review with SRE, runtime, and metrics teams
2026-03-11 10:00 UTC: Autoscaler policy retrospective and final decision meeting
notes: We intentionally moved conservatively on the first mitigation (increase cooldown) because a too-large cooldown increases cost. The long-term fix is multi-signal policies and metric reliability rather than arbitrarily long cooldowns. Several customers asked for SLA credits; support and finance will coordinate. We'll track cost-vs-reliability tradeoffs in a follow-up.
postmortem_review_status: Reviewed by Eng leads 2026-03-02; accepted and action items triaged into next two cycles.
